subject: POC: Pinecone + S3 tiering + pgvector fallback — integration plan and MAP
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@pinecone.io>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call: POC proposal — Pinecone + S3 tiering

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the call today — we walked through Redwood's serving patterns and it looks like a short POC will validate both: 1) using Pinecone as the primary vector store for low-latency retrieval, and 2) pushing cold embeddings / raw objects to an S3 tier for cost savings (and a pgvector fallback for on-prem).

Suggested POC scope (high level):
- 4 weeks, small production-like workload (10k to 100k vectors ingest)
- Demo: Top-K search latency at 512 token contexts; write throughput test (upserts)
- Validate S3 tiering pipeline: snapshot export/import, cold retrieval path + partial rehydration
- Integration points: Redwood SDK connector (indexing hooks), suggested schema for metadata (tenant_id, model_hash, chunk_id)

I've attached a brief ops doc and sample spec: pinecone-technical-ops.pdf, sample-mspoc-specs.xlsx.

Questions for you / Redwood engineering:
- What are your desired latency SLOs for the fast path? (P95/P99 targets)
- Any constraints on KV cache behavior if we use prefix caching?

If this looks good we'll loop in StorageCo (S3 partner) for the tiering architecture and propose a mutual action plan. Happy to join an engineering sync next week.

Best,
Alex Johnson
Partnerships, Pinecone
alex.j@pinecone.io

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@pinecone.io>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:24:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: POC proposal — Pinecone + S3 tiering

Alex — thanks, that summary is helpful.

A few quick answers and context from Redwood's side:
- Target SLOs for the fast path: P95 < 80ms, P99 < 220ms for single-tenant queries in our Dedicated environment (these are what customers expect; Hosted tiers have looser numbers).
- KV cache: we use per-request KV cache plus prefix caching in our runtime; we'd want to test warm vs cold scenarios explicitly.
- In terms of data model, the tenant_id/model_hash/chunk_id you suggested looks right. We'll also pass along embedding versioning metadata so we can detect regressions.

Camila, can you review the ops doc and confirm where the connector would instrument KV caching and rehydration paths? Marcus, I looped you because we'll want to align on go-to-market (co-marketing + sales credits) if the POC is positive.

Next steps:
- Camila to confirm technical checklist and required Pinecone API features (upsert batching, snapshot export).
- Alex to introduce StorageCo S3 contact for tiering design.
- We should draft a 4-week MAP with milestones and success criteria.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.j@pinecone.io>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 11:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: POC proposal — Pinecone + S3 tiering

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 15:12, Alex Johnson <alex.j@pinecone.io> wrote:
> Suggested POC scope (high level):
> - 4 weeks, small production-like workload (10k to 100k vectors ingest)

Thanks, Alex. Quick engineering notes after I skimmed the attachments: good baseline. I'm adding a short checklist (attached: rdw-internal-poc-checklist.md) — highlights below:

Technical checklist / open items:
- Indexing: confirm per-vector metadata size and whether Pinecone preserves arbitrary JSON metadata on export snapshots (we rely on metadata for rehydration).
- Upsert batching: we need 5k+ upsert per second sustained during the ingest step for realistic throughput tests. Please confirm your bulk API limits and recommended client-side batching size.
- Snapshot export: must include vector ids + metadata; StorageCo must be able to read/restore snapshots into S3 with object-level manifests (not opaque blobs).
- Cold path: define expected rehydration latency from S3 to warm store (we'll simulate cache misses at scale).
- Fallback to pgvector: We'll validate a 'graceful degrade' plan (small self-hosted pgvector cluster) — confirm export format compatibility.

Test data and harness:
- We'll provide a synthetic dataset (100k vectors) and a small production trace to replay queries (qps profile).
- Please provide: example index size for 100k items, average vector dimension, and snapshot size estimate.

If Pinecone can confirm upsert limits and snapshot semantics we'll draft the MAP.

Camila Reyes
Staff SWE, Serving Runtime
camila_reyes@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@pinecone.io>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: S3 Sales <s3-sales@storageco.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 08:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: POC proposal — Pinecone + S3 tiering

Camila / Grace — thanks for the specificity. Quick replies inline: 

- Upsert batching: Pinecone bulk upsert supports client-side batches up to 10k vectors per request; we recommend 2k-5k per batch for steady ingestion. We can sustain the ingest you described in a POC.
- Snapshot exports include vector ids + metadata as a newline-delimited JSON manifest and compressed object payloads. StorageCo should be able to read and place these into an S3 bucket with an object manifest.
- Rehydration: typical full-item rehydrate from S3 into warm store ~400–800ms depending on object size; we can instrument the latency path for the POC and add a simple prefetching layer.
- pgvector fallback: export manifests are straightforward to map to pgvector inserts (we've helped other vendors with a small adaptor script).

Hi S3 team (cc'd) — could you share the expected time-to-read for objects in a standard lifecycle (S3 Standard → Glacier transition not part of POC) and any recommended manifest layout for efficient partial restores?

I've uploaded a short design sketch here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1ABCdefGHIjk

Next: I'll put together a draft MAP and calendar for a kickoff engineering workshop week of Dec 13.

Alex Johnson
Partnerships, Pinecone
alex.j@pinecone.io

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@pinecone.io>, S3 Sales <s3-sales@storageco.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Redwood / Pinecone / StorageCo — MAP & next steps (RDWD-7581)

Alex, S3 team — thanks for moving quickly. Per the thread above, here's a concise mutual action plan (attached: MAP-v1.pdf) and the immediate asks so we can lock dates and resources: 

1) Confirm POC dates and participants by EOD Dec 10 (we're proposing kickoff Dec 13).
2) Pinecone: share an example manifest for a 100k-vector snapshot and confirm upsert throttling in writing.
3) StorageCo: confirm expected object restore latencies for objects of ~200KB and a preferred manifest layout.
4) Redwood: we'll supply synthetic dataset + replay harness; Camila will own test harness integration.

Commercial note: linked HubSpot deal RDWD-7581 (https://hubspot.redwood.com/deals/RDWD-7581). Marcus / Grace — please flag any commercial constraints (credits, NDAs).

Proposed scheduling: engineering workshop (2 hours) + integration sprint board. I'll send a calendar invite once we have confirmations.

Action owners:
- Pinecone (Alex): manifest sample, upsert limits (due Dec 10)
- StorageCo (S3 Sales): restore latencies + manifest guidance (due Dec 10)
- Redwood (Camila): test harness + smoke tests (kickoff week)

Thanks — looking forward to getting this live.

Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
